projects.name: vsim - deterministic code-first 3D video (pure-TS software rasterizer)
projects.stack: TypeScript monorepo, pnpm, zod; @vsim/engine-software pure-TS rasterizer; @vsim/engine-three optional GPU engine

verified_results.install: pnpm 9.15.0 via npm -g; pnpm install + pnpm build (all 12 packages) succeeded here
verified_results.extrapolation: a 30s 1080x1920@30 clip = 900 frames ~= 30 min single-worker, ~23 min with 2
verified_results.gotcha: requires ffmpeg on PATH; the spawn failure surfaces as a misleading 'write EPIPE', not a clear error

projects.quality_observed: cube: correct PBR shading, soft contact shadows, supersampled edges. manga: honest cel shading + ink outlines. mouse: crude primitive character (spheres/capsules), far below the reference-zach quality bar.
projects.decision: ADOPT THE ARCHITECTURE, NOT THE RUNTIME. Same fundamental design as our studio (software raster -> raw RGBA -> ffmpeg pipe), but 14x slower at 1080x1920 than our Skia path because every pixel is written in JS. Its scene-document/pacing ideas are worth stealing; its renderer is not worth embedding.

projects.correction: An earlier claim in this repo that neural TTS was blocked by 'onnxruntime-node postinstall downloading from a CDN' was WRONG. The native runtime installs fine from the npm tarball. The real and only blocker is the ~327MB model weights, which live exclusively on blocked hosts.
projects.decision: KEEP AS THE PREFERRED VOICE ADAPTER. One unblock (weights available locally, or one open host) switches the voice from formant synthesis to neural. Code path is ready.

integration_decisions.decision: Do NOT adopt a browser-based render pipeline (HyperFrames/Remotion/three.js-in-Chrome)
integration_decisions.reason: no Chromium obtainable in the build environment; a pipeline that cannot render is not a pipeline

integration_decisions.decision: Adopt software-raster 3D into the existing Skia canvas pipeline instead of embedding vsim
integration_decisions.reason: measured 123-148 ms/frame at 1080x1920 vs vsim 2040 ms/frame (14x); preserves the working pipeline and its QA gate

integration_decisions.decision: Port the lighting recipe (ACES + key/rim/hemisphere + contact shadows) from claude-animation-skills template.html
integration_decisions.reason: it is the difference between flat rectangles and material response; recipe is licence-compatible (MIT) and implementation-independent

integration_decisions.decision: Keep Kokoro as the designated neural-voice adapter behind the existing audio:voice capability
integration_decisions.reason: runtime verified working; only model weights are unreachable. Swapping the adapter changes one line when weights become available.

failures_and_limitations: No Chromium: HyperFrames, Remotion, Playwright, three.js-in-browser all unrunnable here.
No model weights: neural TTS and ASR caption verification blocked (HF + GitHub release CDN both 000).
headless-gl unusable: node-gyp needs Node headers from nodejs.org (TLS disconnect) and can never link.
vsim is 14x slower than the Skia path at 1080x1920 and its example character quality is crude.
The ported rasterizer is box-only: no arbitrary meshes, no skeletal rigs, no texture mapping yet.
Vertical 9:16 framing is width-bound: a 4.6-unit-wide set needs a 16.6-unit camera distance at fov 30. Sets must be narrow and tall.
future_experiments: Add arbitrary triangle meshes + texture sampling to render3d.mjs (mesh loader from glTF/OBJ).
Port PCF shadow mapping (vs js-renderer approach) for real cast shadows instead of projected blobs.
Add a cel/toon shading mode (stepped light ramp + ink outline) for the manga look.
Implement difflib script-alignment captions (words.py follow_script) once an ASR model is available.
Evaluate @drawcall/animate verbs if a WebGL path ever becomes available.
Benchmark the box rasterizer against vsim on a shared scene for a fair speed comparison.
environment_constraints: api.github.com returns 200; contents API inlines file bodies as base64 up to 1,000,000 bytes -> repo stills can be decoded to disk and viewed directly
codeload.github.com tarballs return 200 -> whole repos cloneable without git protocol
arxiv.org PDFs are text-parseable by the page fetcher (tested: 2308.04079, 11 chunks)
PDF: text yes via page fetcher; no pdftotext/pdftoppm locally, so no page-image rendering of local PDFs
SVG viewable only after rasterisation via @napi-rs/canvas loadImage(Buffer)
Audio not listenable; spectrogram/waveform images are viewable but are not hearing
Motion not watchable; frames sampled via ffmpeg -ss / fps+tile storyboard are the only motion evidence
